title: U.S. Bombers Leave a Base in England
summary:
The U.S. Air Force has brought its bombers home from RAF Fairford, an air base in England, the Associated Press reports. The move came after British police looked into a suspected plan to attack the base.

RAF Fairford is about 100 miles west of London. Big American planes called B-52 and B-1 bombers have flown from there since the U.S. war with Iran began. On Sunday, people saw many B-1 bombers fly away.

In late September, police dealt with a security problem at the base. Last week, a man was arrested in London. In all, six people were taken in by police and later let go while the case continues. British officials linked the problem to Iran's government. Iran says it was not involved.

President Donald Trump is deciding what to do next about Iran. More U.S. ships, including an aircraft carrier, are heading to the Middle East.
why_it_matters: It shows how security worries can change where a country keeps its military planes, and it connects to a conflict the U.S. is involved in.
